_source: Role privileges.docx (41-row Activity x Role matrix), applied 2026-09-04
_rules: EXHAUSTIVE: any privilege not listed here is OFF for that role.
'Record/Report, View' includes that page's PDF/Excel export.
Deviations from the document are recorded in each role's _notes.

Only the 83 node ids present in FEATURE_TO_PERMISSION_MAP actually grant anything; the other 45 tree nodes are enforced-only and are NOT listed here. A page still reachable through its sidebar item's primary permission is noted on the role.

Dashboard is on ALL SIX roles by operator decision (2026-09-04) even though the document lists it for none. It is always the first menu item. ADMIN is the only role without CYCLE_READ, so it is the only one whose dashboard shows no filter statistics.

ADMIN._doc: Login, Logout, Notifications, Password change, Audit Trail, User management, Password policies, Backup management
ADMIN._sidebarOrderNote: This array is ORDERED and drives the rendered menu order (sidebar.tsx builds an orderIndex from it; anything absent falls to the end in declaration order). Operator-specified 2026-09-04.
_notes: No audit.export: doc row 33 'Audit Trail Record/Report' is Manager+QA only, while row 32 'Audit Trail View' includes Admin. The document distinguishes them, so Admin views but does not export.
No users.delete: row 7 lists add / active / inactive / password reset / edit - not delete.

OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-04, AFTER the first pass: Admin Requests and Dashboard were restored to ADMIN. Neither appears in the document, so this is a deliberate addition on top of it - the only role that has either. admin_requests.approve / .reject must be toggled EXPLICITLY: the admin-requests sidebar item opts OUT of sidebar auto-grant (primaryPermsForSidebarItem returns [] for it) precisely because its only privileges are ACTION perms, and auto-granting an action perm on menu-enable makes it un-revokable.
Only dashboard.view granted, not create / manage / assign - viewing dashboards is what was asked for.

Enforced-only ids removed from this list because no toggle grants them (they are not among the 83 configurable privileges): notifications.mark. Each corresponding page stays reachable through its sidebar item's primary permission.
BACKUP_MANAGE deliberately not granted: all three backup routes gate on BACKUP_EXPORT / BACKUP_RESTORE, both of which are granted, so BACKUP_MANAGE would be a redundant broader perm.

SUPERVISOR._doc: My Task, Filters View+Upload, PM View+Upload, Replacement View+Upload, Retirement View+Activity, Equipment Groups, Reports, Cleaning Record, Lifecycle, QNN, RFID Track, Deviations. NO Audit Trail.
_notes: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-04, AFTER the first pass: Dashboard added (the document lists it for no role). Placed first, matching every other role. This role holds CYCLE_READ, so the dashboard's filter statistic tiles load with real data.

filters.operate / filters.bypass / filters.rfid_manage kept by operator decision - the tablet needs FILTER_OPERATE and FILTER_RFID_MANAGE for Cleaning Operations and RFID Assign (Tab Operations rows 37, 39).
pm.resubmit kept: a QA rejection would otherwise strand the entry with nobody able to resubmit it. The document has no resubmit row.
Audit Trail, Approvals (block change), and every filter create/edit/hierarchy privilege dropped: not in the document.

Enforced-only ids removed from this list because no toggle grants them (they are not among the 83 configurable privileges): deviations.export, deviations.view, notifications.mark, replacement.view, retirement.view, rfid_track.export, rfid_track.view. Each corresponding page stays reachable through its sidebar item's primary permission.

MANAGER._doc: Audit Trail, Filters View, PM View+Review, Replacement View+Review, Retirement View+Activity, Equipment Groups, Reports, Cleaning Record, Lifecycle, QNN, RFID Track, Audit View+Report, Deviations. NO My Task.
MANAGER._sidebarOrderNote: Operator-specified 2026-09-04: Dashboard, Filters, PM Schedules, Replacement List, Retirement List, Equipment Groups, Reports, Notifications, Audit Trail. 'Reports' is a COLLAPSIBLE GROUP, not a sidebar id - sidebar.tsx inserts it at the position of its FIRST VISIBLE CHILD, so all five children (cleaning-cycles, filter-lifecycle-report, quality-notifications, rfid-track-record, deviations) must sit between equipment-groups and notifications. Their order inside this array is also the order inside the group.
_notes: pm.edit / pm.edit_entry dropped: not in the document.

OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-04, AFTER the first pass: Dashboard added (the document lists it for no role). Placed first, matching ADMIN. Unlike ADMIN, MANAGER holds CYCLE_READ, so the dashboard's filter statistic tiles actually load for this role.

pm.reject dropped: it is enforced-only AND its grant set is PM_APPROVE - enabling "Reject PM Schedule" would have handed MANAGER the approve permission the document reserves for QA.
